blocks.html: At-Home vs. In-Office Dry Eye Treatments

blocks.text: When Dry Eyes Need More Than Basic Eye Drops
blocks.html: When Dry Eyes Need More Than Basic Eye Drops

[[b]][[a href="https://www.briargroveeye.com/eye-care-services/eye-conditions/dry-eye-disease-and-treatment/"]]Dry eye syndrome[[/a]] [[/b]]varies from person to person. Some patients mainly notice redness and irritation, while others struggle more with blurry vision or burning sensations later in the day.
[[b]]Uptown Houston’s[[/b]] heat, heavy air conditioning use, and long hours spent on digital devices can all contribute to worsening symptoms over time.

blocks.text: At-Home Care for Dry Eye Symptoms
blocks.html: At-Home Care for Dry Eye Symptoms
Home remedies can help many patients manage mild irritation and support healthier tear quality between visits.
Warm Compresses & Eyelid Hygiene
Warm compresses help loosen oils trapped inside the eyelid glands. Regular eyelid hygiene may also reduce irritation linked to debris and inflammation around the lashes and lid margins.
Lubricating Eye Drops

Artificial tears and lubricating drops can temporarily soothe dryness and improve comfort during reading, travel, or extended screen use. Some patients benefit from preservative-free drops when symptoms occur more frequently throughout the day.

blocks.text: Daily Habits That Support Eye Comfort
blocks.html: Daily Habits That Support Eye Comfort
Small adjustments may help reduce irritation and support tear stability:

items: Taking screen breaks throughout the day
Blinking more intentionally during computer work

blocks.html: Nutritional Support
Omega-3 fatty acids may help support tear quality and reduce tear evaporation in some patients with chronic dry eye symptoms.
Chronic Dry Eye Care
Persistent dry eye symptoms often need more than surface-level moisture. In-office treatment focuses on improving tear function and identifying underlying causes that continue to trigger irritation.
Comprehensive Evaluation

Dry eye exams help evaluate tear stability, eyelid health, inflammation, and oil gland function. Your [[b]][[a href="https://www.briargroveeye.com/our-eye-doctors/"]]eye doctor[[/a]][[/b]] may perform Tear Break Up Time testing to measure how quickly tears evaporate from the eye’s surface.
Prescription Treatments
Prescription medications may help reduce inflammation or improve natural tear production when over-the-counter products no longer provide enough relief.
Some patients also benefit from short-term therapies designed to calm irritation affecting the ocular surface.
Punctal Plugs
Punctal plugs help slow tear drainage, so natural moisture stays on the eyes longer. This treatment may help patients with more advanced dryness or rapid tear evaporation.
Managing Blepharitis & Eyelid Inflammation

Inflammation around the eyelids often contributes to chronic dry eye symptoms. Treatment may include heated masks, medicated ointments, or specialized eyelid hygiene routines designed to improve comfort and tear quality.

FAQs
[[b]]What causes chronic dry eye?[[/b]]

items: Chronic dry eye can develop from aging, environmental conditions, medications, inflammation, meibomian gland dysfunction, contact lens wear, and prolonged screen use.

blocks.html: [[b]]Can dry eye make vision blurry?[[/b]]

items: Yes. An unstable tear film can interrupt how light enters the eye, causing blurry or fluctuating vision throughout the day.

blocks.html: [[b]]Why do my eyes water when they feel dry?[[/b]]

items: Dry eyes can trigger reflex tearing, where the eyes produce excess tears in response to irritation. These tears often evaporate too quickly to provide lasting comfort.
